description:
## Destination

buck2 is bundled inside turnkey: each turnkey revision ships exactly one **pinned buck2 release** (binary from toolbox's plain `buck2`, an exactly-named prelude, buck2 source rev + protos hash), resolved from turnkey's own toolbox. Consumers no longer declare buck2 in `toolchain.toml`; they only configure turnkey. This effort carries execution: the map is done when that is true in the tree, docs and templates.

## Notes

- **Execution is in scope** (overrides wayfinder's plan-only default): task tickets make the change.
- Settled while charting (2026-09-25):
  - One pin per turnkey revision, a single record in `nix/buck2/buck2-source.nix`; the multi-release table, `matchingPreludeVersion` and the "unsupported buck2 → caching off" path go away. Prelude pinned exactly in the same record.
  - buck2 resolves from turnkey's own toolbox/teller; a consumer's `registry`/`registryExtensions` cannot move it. Only override: flake-input `follows` on toolbox.
  - Only buck2 is bundled; reindeer is not (nothing in turnkey uses it).
  - `buck2`/`buck2-toolchain` in a `toolchain.toml` is a hard evaluation error pointing at the migration note.
  - Which shells get buck2 is a per-shell setting in `flake.nix`, next to `declarationFiles` (turnkey's own docs shell has none).
  - `buck2` stays on PATH. A read-only `turnkey.buck2.version` surfaces the pin (welcome message, docs).
  - Built on top of the unpushed test-result-caching stack (turnkey-vnm); the remaining work of turnkey-q7r (upgrade checklist) folds into this map, rewritten as "how to bump turnkey's buck2 pin".
  - The test-runner parity suite gates every pin bump (CI gate if fast enough).
- Record as an ADR ("turnkey owns the buck2 version") + CONTEXT.md term **Pinned buck2 release**.
- VCS is jj; repo-wide rules in CLAUDE.md apply. Consult /domain-modeling for glossary/ADR work, /codebase-design for module-interface tickets.

## Decisions so far

## Not yet specified

- Implementing the parity-suite bump gate (CI job shape, runner requirements) — hangs on whether it is a CI gate at all.
- Landing order with the test-result-caching stack (turnkey-vnm) and what happens to the parked q7r commit once this map's tickets are stacked on it.
- Whether `nix/buck2/mappings.nix` still needs `buck2`/`buck2-toolchain` skip entries once they are rejected earlier.

## Out of scope

- `buck2.prelude.strategy` escape hatches (`bundled`/`path`/`git`): a separate knob (the prelude, not buck2); left as they are.
- reindeer: not bundled; consumers who want it declare it like any other tool.
title: Bundle buck2 inside turnkey
